# Rank-1 LoRA marker implants are ungated writes: the read direction barely moves from random, B aligns with the marker unembedding row, and plain bank geometry beats the firing predictor in every cell (MODERATE confidence) ## Human TL;DR **Headline.** Pushed the marker implant down to rank 1 — at this rank the read and write vectors are literally a single (a, b) per module, no SVD needed — and the read side barely moves: |cos(a_trained, a_init)| = 0.99 across all 30 cells. The implant is an ungated write, and "a · v_persona" doesn't rank-order who leaks — plain `cos(v_persona, v_source)` from the SAME bank beats it in 0 / 30 cells. **Takeaways.** - The A-init control I couldn't run on #604 settles it cleanly: at the only training window where the marker actually lands (lr 5e-6, band [5,12] nat), A rotates 7-16% of its initial norm. Whatever does the persona selection lives in B + the base prior, not in a learned read direction. - B is consistent with the marker, exactly as #604 predicted: cos(b, W_U[marker]) reaches 0.79 on down_proj and 0.63 on o_proj, max over layers 20-27, vs a frequency-matched null around 0.05. - The firing predictor (a · v_persona scaled by ||b||) is positive 11/12 read cells (median ρ = +0.33), but it loses to plain bank geometry in every cell (median Δρ = −0.33, all 30 losses). The geometry comparator hits ρ ≈ 0.66-0.69 with NO adapter — the persona-similarity signal that orders leakage was already in the base model. - Cross-seed a-instability persists at r=1 (median |cos| = 0.012-0.022, dead at #604's 0.015 rank-16 value). That's the mechanical signature of "random Kaiming start that barely moved" — not seed-arbitrary learning. **How this updates me.** I believe more strongly that the rank-1 leakage model `a·v_c → b·W_marker` is the wrong way to read these adapters at this dose. The implant doesn't gate on persona at all — it pushes the marker direction into a (small) subspace via B and the rest is the base model's own persona geometry doing the bystander ordering. To rescue the "a learns the persona detector" hypothesis I'd need to push to a much higher dose where A actually rotates (the closest-approach trajectory shows it growing slowly), but at that point the source saturates and the experiment loses its variance. *(First pass — Thomas refines this before sending to the mentor.)* ## TL;DR ### Motivation Task [#604](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/604) decomposed 209 trained marker adapters at ranks 8, 16, and 32. The write direction came out seed-stable (median cross-seed |cos| = 0.927) and pointed at the marker; the top-1 key direction was seed-arbitrary (|cos| = 0.015) and did NOT match the persona context vector at either tested token position. That left an unsatisfying ambiguity: was the seed-arbitrary key telling us "the adapter is an ungated write," or was it an artifact of SVD'ing a rank-16 update whose true detector lives somewhere outside the top singular pair? At r=1 there is no SVD ambiguity. The per-module update is exactly the outer product `ΔW = s·b·aᵀ` with `s = α/√r = 8/1 = 8`, so `a` IS the learned read direction and `b` IS the learned write direction. Train at r=1, save the random A at step 0, and you can ask three things that #604 couldn't: 1. Does `a` rotate toward the persona's context vector during training, or does it stay near the random Kaiming start? 2. Does `cos(b, W_U[marker])` match the marker direction (mechanism check)? 3. Does the per-persona firing strength `s·(a·v_c′)` rank-order measured leakage with no free parameters? The literature line — *Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models* (arXiv 2402.16842) — predicts answer (1) is "barely rotates" (a random A performs nearly as well as a trained one). The plan registered that as the pre-registered ungated-write outcome (H2), and treated the firing-vs-leakage Spearman test (H4) as the surprise direction: a positive result there would be the cleanest possible read-side persona-gating result the project has produced. ### What I ran 30 cells of rank-1 LoRA marker implants on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, all band-stopped at source `log P(marker) − base ∈ [5, 12]` nat (the recipe's clean window). The marker is the single token ` ※` (id 83399, leading space) appended to the source persona's own on-policy greedy response. - **Read-side placement (12 cells):** target_modules = (q_proj, v_proj); 4 sources × 3 seeds. Here `a` lives in the post-RMSNorm residual subspace — the right place to compare against the persona context vector with `a∘γ`. - **Write-side placement (12 cells):** target_modules = (o_proj, down_proj); 4 sources × 3 seeds. Here `b` lives in residual space — the right place to compare against the marker unembedding row `W_U[marker]`. - **Bridge placement (6 cells):** target_modules = (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj) at the parent #604 dial's exact placement; 2 sources × 3 seeds. Forces rank to be the ONLY change vs the parent recipe. Sources: florist, medical_doctor, librarian, police_officer. Seeds: 42, 137, 256. Band-stop fired in 30/30 cells; final source ΔlogP per cell ranged 4.44 – 6.11 nat (median 5.20). The A-init snapshot is saved at training step 0 (B is exactly zero by PEFT default; A is Kaiming-uniform). Eval reads `log P(marker)` at the post-response slot on the 19-persona panel × 20 disjoint questions, on-policy greedy R, the four-float storage contract (`logp_marker, z_marker, z_eos, logZ`) on both trained and base sides.
